class Engine:
    def __init__(self, spec: ModelSpec, decode_concurrency: int = 4, prompt_concurrency: int = 2,
                 prompt_cache_size: int = 8, prompt_cache_bytes: int | None = None, reserve_gb: float = 6.0,
                 disk_cache_gb: float = 20.0, guards: bool = True):
        self.spec = spec
        self.guards = guards
        ns = argparse.Namespace(
            model=spec.path, adapter_path=spec.adapter, draft_model=None, num_draft_tokens=3, trust_remote_code=False,
            chat_template="", use_default_chat_template=False, temp=spec.temperature, top_p=spec.top_p,
            top_k=spec.top_k, min_p=0.0, max_tokens=32000, chat_template_args={},
            decode_concurrency=decode_concurrency, prompt_concurrency=prompt_concurrency, prefill_step_size=512,
            prompt_cache_size=prompt_cache_size, prompt_cache_bytes=prompt_cache_bytes, kv_bits=None,
            kv_group_size=64, quantized_kv_start=DEFAULT_QUANTIZED_KV_START, pipeline=False, allowed_origins=["*"],
        )
        self.provider = mls.ModelProvider(ns)
        cache = MovingPromptCache(prompt_cache_size, prompt_cache_bytes or (1 << 63))
        # The generator thread loads the model, so all MLX work stays on one thread and stream.
        self.generator = mls.ResponseGenerator(self.provider, cache)
        tokenize = self.generator._tokenize

        def tokenize_and_track(*a, **k):
            # Runs on the generation thread before the prompt is read, so a mid-request snapshot can't beat it.
            tokenized = merge_prompt_tail(tokenize(*a, **k))
            cache.reading = cache.reading[-15:] + [tokenized[0]]
            return tokenized

        self.generator._tokenize = tokenize_and_track
        while self.provider.tokenizer is None:
            if not self.generator.generation_available():
                raise RuntimeError(f"could not load {spec.path}")
            time.sleep(0.2)
        self.tokenizer = self.provider.tokenizer
        if spec.kv_bits:  # before any request makes a cache
            quantize_kv(self.provider.model, spec.kv_bits)
        cache.decode = self.tokenizer.decode
        self.budget_tokens = BudgetTokens(self.tokenizer)
        self.loop_exempt = loop_exempt_ids(self.tokenizer)
        self.cache = cache
        self.generator.on_stop = cache.flush
        try:
            self.max_context = self._context_that_fits()
        except NotEnoughMemory:
            self.generator.stop_and_join()  # its thread holds the loaded model
            raise
        self._fit_memory(cache, ns, prompt_cache_bytes, reserve_gb)
        if disk_cache_gb > 0:
            disk = DiskCache(home() / "cache", spec.path, int(disk_cache_gb * (1 << 30)), spec.adapter, spec.kv_bits)
            key = self.provider.model_key
            restored = disk.restore(lambda t, c, kind: LRUPromptCache.insert_cache(cache, key, t, c, cache_type=kind),
                                    cache.max_bytes)
            cache.disk = disk
            if restored:
                logging.info("restored %.1f GB of prompt caches from disk", restored / (1 << 30))
        threading.Thread(target=self._watch, daemon=True).start()
        logging.info("loaded %s%s (thinking=%s, tools=%s, think-end id=%s, KV cache %s)", spec.path,
                     f" + adapter {spec.adapter}" if spec.adapter else "", self.tokenizer.has_thinking,
                     self.tokenizer.has_tool_calling, self.budget_tokens.end_id,
                     f"{spec.kv_bits}-bit" if spec.kv_bits else "full precision")

    def _kv_bytes_per_token(self) -> int | None:
        try:
            layers = sum(isinstance(c, (KVCache, QuantizedKVCache)) for c in self.provider.model.make_cache())
            path = Path(self.spec.path)
            if not (path / "config.json").is_file():
                return None
            _, heads, head_dim = _kv_shape(json.loads((path / "config.json").read_text()))
            return kv_bytes_per_token(layers, heads, head_dim, self.spec.kv_bits) if layers else None
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  an unusual model: no memory-derived context limit
            return None

    def _context_that_fits(self) -> int | None:
        """A context limit this machine can hold. Past it the server answers "prompt is too long" (Claude Code then
        compacts the conversation) instead of running out of memory mid-turn."""
        weights = sum(v.nbytes for _, v in tree_flatten(self.provider.model.parameters()))
        limit = mx.device_info()["max_recommended_working_set_size"]
        per_token = self._kv_bytes_per_token()
        if per_token is None:
            check_memory(self.spec.name, limit, weights)
            return None
        self.cache.kv_bytes_per_token = per_token
        fits = context_that_fits(limit, weights, per_token, overhead=CONTEXT_OVERHEAD)
        logging.info("memory: about %d tokens of context fit (%d KB of KV cache per token; model allows %s)", fits,
                     per_token // 1024, self.spec.context or "unknown")
        check_memory(self.spec.name, limit, weights, fits)
        return fits

    def _fit_memory(self, cache, ns, prompt_cache_bytes, reserve_gb):
        """Size the prompt cache and MLX's buffer pool to what the GPU can hold beside the weights: unbounded,
        saved prompt caches and freed buffers grow until Metal runs out of memory mid-generation."""
        gb = 1 << 30
        weights = sum(v.nbytes for _, v in tree_flatten(self.provider.model.parameters()))
        limit = mx.device_info()["max_recommended_working_set_size"]
        spare = limit - weights - int(reserve_gb * gb)
        # The cap covers saved caches plus the caches active sequences hold (mlx-lm trims the LRU to the cap minus the
        # active bytes). Too small, and a long conversation is evicted after every turn and re-read from scratch; the
        # reserve covers prefill's attention scratch, which grows with context length.
        if prompt_cache_bytes is None:
            prompt_cache_bytes = max(spare, gb // 2)
        cache.max_bytes = ns.prompt_cache_bytes = prompt_cache_bytes
        mx.set_cache_limit(max(min(spare // 8, gb), gb // 4))
        logging.info("memory: GPU limit %.1f GB, weights %.1f GB, prompt cache up to %.1f GB, %.1f GB reserved for "
                     "active sequences", limit / gb, weights / gb, prompt_cache_bytes / gb, reserve_gb)
        if spare < gb:
            logging.warning("this model leaves under 1 GB beside its weights; long contexts may run out of memory")

    def _watch(self):
        """mlx-lm's generation thread can't recover from a Metal failure (out of memory, most often). A server that
        stays up after it dies only fails every request, so exit and let whatever started it start it again."""
        while self.generator.generation_available():
            time.sleep(1)
        logging.critical("the generation engine stopped (see the error above); exiting")
        os._exit(70)

    def adapt_memory(self, headroom_gb: float = 2.5):
        """After a request: if memory came within `headroom_gb` of the GPU limit, shrink the prompt cache by the
        overshoot. A fixed reserve can't be right for every Mac, model and context length; this settles on what the
        machine actually needs after its first long session."""
        gb = 1 << 30
        peak, limit = mx.get_peak_memory(), mx.device_info()["max_recommended_working_set_size"]
        mx.reset_peak_memory()
        cap = shrink_cap(self.cache.max_bytes, peak, limit, int(headroom_gb * gb))
        if cap < self.cache.max_bytes:
            self.cache.max_bytes = self.provider.cli_args.prompt_cache_bytes = cap
            logging.warning("memory peaked at %.1f of %.1f GB; prompt cache lowered to %.1f GB", peak / gb, limit / gb,
                            cap / gb)

    @staticmethod
    def memory() -> str:
        gb = 1 << 30
        return (f"mem active={mx.get_active_memory() / gb:.1f}G peak={mx.get_peak_memory() / gb:.1f}G "
                f"pool={mx.get_cache_memory() / gb:.1f}G")

    def count_tokens(self, plan: Plan) -> int:
        return len(self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(plan.messages, tools=plan.tools, add_generation_prompt=True,
                                                      tokenize=True, **plan.template_kwargs))

    def run(self, plan: Plan, on_progress: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None) -> Run:
        budget: list[ThinkBudget] = []
        guard: list[LoopGuard] = []

        def extra():
            procs = []
            if self.guards:
                # Ahead of the budget: a token the budget forces replaces the logits whole, so it stays possible.
                guard.append(LoopGuard(self.loop_exempt))
                procs.append(guard[-1])
            b = self.budget_tokens.make(plan.think_budget)
            if b is not None:
                budget.append(b)
                procs.append(b)
            return procs

        args = _Args(
            model=mls.ModelDescription(model="default_model", draft="default_model", adapter=None),
            sampling=mls.SamplingArguments(temperature=plan.temperature, top_p=plan.top_p, top_k=plan.top_k,
                                           min_p=0.0, xtc_probability=0.0, xtc_threshold=0.0),
            logits=mls.LogitsProcessorArguments(logit_bias=None, repetition_penalty=0.0, repetition_context_size=20,
                                                presence_penalty=0.0, presence_context_size=20,
                                                frequency_penalty=0.0, frequency_context_size=20),
            stop_words=plan.stop, max_tokens=plan.max_tokens, num_draft_tokens=3, logprobs=False, top_logprobs=0,
            seed=None, chat_template_kwargs=plan.template_kwargs,
            extra_processors=extra,
        )
        request = mls.CompletionRequest(request_type="chat", prompt="", messages=plan.messages, tools=plan.tools,
                                        role_mapping=None)
        ctx, responses = self.generator.generate(request, args, progress_callback=on_progress)

        def pieces():
            try:
                yield from _classify(ctx, responses, lambda: bool(guard) and guard[0].gave_up)
            finally:
                self.cache.reading = [p for p in self.cache.reading if p != ctx.prompt]

        return Run(prompt_tokens=len(ctx.prompt), cached_tokens=max(ctx.prompt_cache_count, 0),
                   tool_parser=ctx.tool_parser, pieces=pieces(), stop=ctx.stop, budget=budget, guard=guard)


def _classify(ctx, responses, gave_up: Callable[[], bool] = lambda: False):
    """Split generated text into reasoning / normal / tool pieces with mlx-lm's state machine, which also strips
    the control markers (<think>, <tool_call> ...). A response the loop guard gave up on ends here as if it had hit
    the token cap: generation stops, and the client sees a "length" finish."""
    sm = ctx.text_sm.make_state(ctx.initial_state)
    n = 0
    for gen in responses:
        n += 1
        if gen.finish_reason == "stop":
            sm, state = TextStateMachine.discard(sm)
            segments = [(state, "")]
        elif gen.finish_reason == "length" or gave_up():
            sm, segments = TextStateMachine.split(sm, gen.text)
            sm, flushed, state = TextStateMachine.flush(sm)
            segments.append((state, flushed))
            if gen.finish_reason != "length":
                ctx.stop()
                yield [Piece(s, t) for s, t in segments], "length", n
                return
        else:
            sm, segments = TextStateMachine.split(sm, gen.text)
        yield [Piece(s, t) for s, t in segments], gen.finish_reason, n


# ===== translate.py =====
"""Anthropic Messages request -> chat-template input and generation settings."""

import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .config import EFFORTS, ModelSpec
from .guards import STUCK_REPEATS, stuck_call_note, stuck_call_repeats
from .stream import PROGRESS_NOTE


class RequestError(ValueError):
    """The request is malformed; reported to the client as invalid_request_error."""


@dataclass
class Plan:
    messages: list[dict]
    tools: list[dict] | None
    template_kwargs: dict
    max_tokens: int
    stop: list[str]
    temperature: float
    top_p: float
    top_k: int
    think_budget: int
    thinking: bool
    effort: str
    hidden_tools: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    # Deferred tools loaded mid-conversation: described where they were loaded, not in `tools` (see convert_tools).
    loaded_tools: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    context: int | None = None
    context_capped: bool = False  # max_tokens was cut to fit the context window
    stuck_repeats: int = 0  # the request ends with this many identical tool steps, and got a reminder about it


def parse_tools(p: "Plan") -> list[dict] | None:
    """Every tool the model may call: the listed ones plus deferred ones loaded so far."""
    return (p.tools or []) + p.loaded_tools or None


class PromptTooLong(RequestError):
    """Worded exactly as the Anthropic API words it: Claude Code matches the text to start compacting."""

    def __init__(self, tokens: int, maximum: int):
        super().__init__(f"prompt is too long: {tokens} tokens > {maximum} maximum")


MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 1024  # a prompt that leaves less room than this is too long to answer usefully


def fit_context(p: "Plan", prompt_tokens: int) -> None:
    """Shrink max_tokens so prompt + output fits the context window, as the Anthropic API does."""
    if not p.context:
        return
    room = p.context - prompt_tokens
    if room < MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS:
        raise PromptTooLong(prompt_tokens, p.context - MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS)
    if p.max_tokens > room:
        p.max_tokens, p.context_capped = room, True


def _text(content, defs: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """Flatten a string or a list of content blocks to text."""
    if content is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    parts = []
    for block in content:
        kind = block.get("type")
        if kind == "text":
            parts.append(block.get("text", ""))
        elif kind == "image":
            parts.append("[image omitted: this model cannot see images]")
        elif kind == "tool_reference":
            name = block.get("tool_name", "")
            spec = (defs or {}).get(name)
            parts.append(f"Tool {name} is now available." + (f" Its definition:\n{json.dumps(spec)}" if spec else ""))
        elif kind == "document":
            parts.append(_text(block.get("source", {}).get("content"), defs) or "[document omitted]")
    return "\n".join(p for p in parts if p)


def _loaded_tools(messages) -> set[str]:
    """Deferred tools that a tool result has referenced (Claude Code's tool search loads them this way)."""
    names = set()
    for m in messages:
        if isinstance(m.get("content"), list):
            for block in m["content"]:
                if block.get("type") == "tool_result" and isinstance(block.get("content"), list):
                    names.update(b.get("tool_name") for b in block["content"] if b.get("type") == "tool_reference")
    return names


BILLING_LINE = re.compile(r"^x-anthropic-billing-header:[^\n]*\n?", re.MULTILINE)


def _without_billing_line(text: str) -> str:
    """Claude Code opens its system prompt with a usage-attribution line whose suffix changes between requests; the
    model has no use for it, and mid-prompt it would make every later token miss the prompt cache."""
    return BILLING_LINE.sub("", text).strip("\n")


def convert_messages(system, messages, defs: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    sys_text = _without_billing_line(_text(system))
    if sys_text:
        out.append({"role": "system", "content": sys_text})
    for m in messages:
        role, content = m.get("role"), m.get("content")
        if role == "system":
            # Claude Code sends mid-conversation system messages; most chat templates only allow a system
            # message first, so later ones become reminders inside the conversation.
            text = _text(content)
            if not out:
                out.append({"role": "system", "content": text})
            elif out[-1]["role"] == "system" and len(out) == 1:
                out[0]["content"] += "\n\n" + text
            elif text:
                out.append({"role": "user", "content": f"<system-reminder>\n{text}\n</system-reminder>"})
            continue
        if role not in ("user", "assistant"):
            raise RequestError(f"unsupported message role: {role!r}")
        if isinstance(content, str):
            out.append({"role": role, "content": content})
            continue
        if not isinstance(content, list):
            raise RequestError("message content must be a string or a list of blocks")
        if role == "user":
            pending = []
            for block in content:
                if block.get("type") == "tool_result":
                    if pending:
                        out.append({"role": "user", "content": "\n".join(pending)}); pending = []
                    text = _text(block.get("content"), defs)
                    if block.get("is_error") and "error" not in text[:40].lower():
                        text = f"Error: {text}"
                    out.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": block.get("tool_use_id"), "content": text})
                else:
                    t = _text([block])
                    if t:
                        pending.append(t)
            if pending:
                out.append({"role": "user", "content": "\n".join(pending)})
        else:
            msg = {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}
            reasoning, texts, calls = [], [], []
            for block in content:
                kind = block.get("type")
                if kind == "thinking":
                    thought = PROGRESS_NOTE.sub("", block.get("thinking", ""))
                    if thought.strip():
                        reasoning.append(thought)
                elif kind == "text":
                    texts.append(block.get("text", ""))
                elif kind == "tool_use":
                    calls.append({"id": block.get("id"), "type": "function",
                                  "function": {"name": block.get("name"), "arguments": block.get("input") or {}}})
            msg["content"] = "\n\n".join(t for t in texts if t)
            if reasoning:
                msg["reasoning_content"] = "\n\n".join(reasoning)
            if calls:
                msg["tool_calls"] = calls
            out.append(msg)
    return out


def convert_tools(tools, messages) -> tuple[list[dict] | None, list[str], list[dict]]:
    """(listed tools, names of deferred tools not loaded, deferred tools loaded). Loaded deferred tools stay out of
    the listed ones: chat templates render the list at the top of the prompt, so a tool joining it mid-conversation
    changes the prompt's first tokens and the whole conversation is re-read (20k tokens, minutes, on a local model).
    Their definitions go where tool search loaded them instead."""
    if not tools:
        return None, [], []
    loaded = _loaded_tools(messages)
    out, hidden, late = [], [], []
    for t in tools:
        if "input_schema" not in t:  # server-side tools (web search etc.) can't run locally
            continue
        fn = {"type": "function", "function": {"name": t["name"], "description": t.get("description", ""),
                                               "parameters": t["input_schema"]}}
        if t.get("defer_loading"):
            if t["name"] in loaded:
                late.append(fn)
            else:
                hidden.append(t["name"])
            continue
        out.append(fn)
    return out or None, hidden, late


def plan(body: dict, spec: ModelSpec, default_max: int = 32000, guards: bool = True) -> Plan:
    if not isinstance(body.get("messages"), list) or not body["messages"]:
        raise RequestError("messages must be a non-empty list")
    # As in Anthropic's API, a request thinks only when it asks to. Claude Code asks on every turn of its agent loop
    # ("adaptive") and leaves thinking out of its side requests, such as summarizing a page WebFetch read, which a
    # reasoning model would otherwise spend minutes thinking through.
    thinking_cfg = body.get("thinking") or {}
    thinking = thinking_cfg.get("type", "disabled") != "disabled"
    effort = (body.get("output_config") or {}).get("effort") or "high"
    if effort not in EFFORTS:
        raise RequestError(f"unknown effort {effort!r}")

    kwargs = dict(spec.template_kwargs)
    kwargs["enable_thinking"] = thinking
    if spec.effort_kwarg and thinking:
        kwargs[spec.effort_kwarg] = spec.effort_map.get(effort, effort)

    budget = spec.budget_for(effort) if thinking else 0
    if thinking and thinking_cfg.get("budget_tokens"):
        budget = int(thinking_cfg["budget_tokens"])
    elif budget and _continues_tool_loop(body["messages"]):
        budget = max(int(budget * spec.followup_budget), MIN_FOLLOWUP_BUDGET)

    max_tokens = int(body.get("max_tokens") or default_max)
    tools, hidden, late = convert_tools(body.get("tools"), body["messages"])
    messages = convert_messages(body.get("system"), body["messages"], {f["function"]["name"]: f for f in late})
    tools, messages = _apply_tool_choice(body.get("tool_choice"), tools, messages, late)
    # A model stuck repeating one tool call gets told so before it answers (guards.py). The reminder goes last, so
    # the prompt cache still covers everything before it.
    stuck = stuck_call_repeats(body["messages"]) if guards else 0
    if stuck >= STUCK_REPEATS:
        messages = messages + [{"role": "user",
                                "content": f"<system-reminder>\n{stuck_call_note(stuck)}\n</system-reminder>"}]
    else:
        stuck = 0
    return Plan(
        messages=messages,
        tools=tools,
        template_kwargs=kwargs,
        max_tokens=max_tokens,
        stop=list(body.get("stop_sequences") or []),
        temperature=float(body["temperature"]) if body.get("temperature") is not None else spec.temperature,
        top_p=float(body["top_p"]) if body.get("top_p") is not None else spec.top_p,
        top_k=int(body["top_k"]) if body.get("top_k") is not None else spec.top_k,
        think_budget=budget,
        thinking=thinking,
        effort=effort,
        hidden_tools=hidden,
        loaded_tools=late,
        context=spec.context,
        stuck_repeats=stuck,
    )


MIN_FOLLOWUP_BUDGET = 512


def _continues_tool_loop(messages) -> bool:
    """The request answers the model's own tool calls (the last message holds tool results and nothing the user
    typed), as opposed to starting work on something the user just asked."""
    last = messages[-1]
    if last.get("role") != "user" or not isinstance(last.get("content"), list):
        return False
    kinds = {b.get("type") for b in last["content"]}
    if "tool_result" not in kinds:
        return False
    typed = [b for b in last["content"] if b.get("type") == "text"
             and not b.get("text", "").lstrip().startswith("<system-reminder>")]
    return not typed


def _apply_tool_choice(choice, tools, messages, late=()):
    """Open models can't be forced to call a tool, so "any" and a named tool become an instruction (and a named
    tool narrows the list); "none" removes the tools."""
    kind = (choice or {}).get("type", "auto")
    if kind == "auto" or not tools:
        return tools, messages
    if kind == "none":
        return None, messages
    if kind == "tool":
        named = [t for t in [*tools, *late] if t["function"]["name"] == choice.get("name")]
        if not named:
            raise RequestError(f"tool_choice names unknown tool {choice.get('name')!r}")
        tools, note = named, f"Respond by calling the {choice['name']} tool."
    elif kind == "any":
        note = "Respond by calling one of the available tools."
    else:
        raise RequestError(f"unknown tool_choice type {kind!r}")
    return tools, messages + [{"role": "user", "content": f"<system-reminder>\n{note}\n</system-reminder>"}]


# ===== http.py =====
"""HTTP front: the Anthropic Messages API over a threading HTTP server."""

import hmac
import json
import logging
import os
import select
import socket
import struct
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from . import __version__
from .config import ModelSpec, resolve
from .engine import Engine
from .stream import MessageBuilder, new_id, progress_note, sse
from .translate import RequestError, fit_context, parse_tools, plan


# Claude Code drops a stream that sends nothing for a few minutes, and a tool call is only sent once it closes, so a
# long Write could go silent; a ping goes out whenever nothing else has for this long.
HEARTBEAT_SECONDS = 5.0
# Claude Code doesn't count pings as activity either, and reading a long prompt can take longer than it waits, so a
# slow prefill reports its progress as a line of thinking (stripped again when the conversation comes back).
PROGRESS_SECONDS = 30.0
DISCONNECT_CHECK_SECONDS = 2.0


class Server(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = True

    def __init__(self, address, engine: Engine, models: dict[str, ModelSpec], api_key: str | None = None,
                 guards: bool = True):
        super().__init__(address, Handler)
        self.engine, self.models, self.api_key, self.guards = engine, models, api_key, guards


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server: Server
    server_version = f"aris-server/{__version__}"

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        logging.debug("%s %s", self.address_string(), fmt % args)

    # --- plumbing -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _json(self, status: int, body: dict):
        data = json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("request-id", new_id("req"))
        self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("content-length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def _error(self, status: int, kind: str, message: str):
        self._json(status, {"type": "error", "error": {"type": kind, "message": message}})

    def _reject(self, e: RequestError):
        # Logged: a "prompt is too long" is what makes Claude Code compact, which is otherwise invisible here.
        logging.info("rejected a request: %s", e)
        return self._error(400, "invalid_request_error", str(e))

    def _authorized(self) -> bool:
        key = self.server.api_key
        if not key:
            return True
        given = self.headers.get("x-api-key") or self.headers.get("authorization", "").removeprefix("Bearer ").strip()
        return hmac.compare_digest(given.encode(), key.encode())

    def _body(self) -> dict | None:
        try:
            n = int(self.headers.get("content-length") or 0)
            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(n) or b"{}")
        except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            self._error(400, "invalid_request_error", "body must be JSON")
            return None
        if not isinstance(body, dict):
            self._error(400, "invalid_request_error", "body must be a JSON object")
            return None
        return body

    def _client_gone(self) -> bool:
        """True once the client has closed its end. A request that is still generating writes nothing (non-streaming,
        or a tool call in progress), so a dropped client would otherwise keep its generation running."""
        try:
            readable, _, _ = select.select([self.connection], [], [], 0)
            return bool(readable) and self.connection.recv(1, socket.MSG_PEEK) == b""
        except OSError:
            return True

    @property
    def route(self) -> str:
        return urlsplit(self.path).path.rstrip("/")

    # --- routes ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def do_GET(self):
        if self.route == "/health":
            return self._json(200, {"status": "ok", "model": self.server.engine.spec.name})
        if not self._authorized():
            return self._error(401, "authentication_error", "invalid x-api-key")
        if self.route == "/v1/models":
            names = [self.server.engine.spec.name] + [n for n in self.server.models if n != self.server.engine.spec.name]
            data = [{"type": "model", "id": n, "display_name": n, "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"} for n in names]
            window = _fit_window(self.server.engine.spec.context, getattr(self.server.engine, "max_context", None))
            if window:
                data[0]["context_window"] = window  # the loaded model's, on this machine: clients compact before it
            return self._json(200, {"data": data, "has_more": False, "first_id": names[0], "last_id": names[-1]})
        self._error(404, "not_found_error", f"no route {self.route}")

    def do_HEAD(self):
        self.send_response(200 if self.route in ("", "/health") else 404)
        self.end_headers()

    def do_POST(self):
        if not self._authorized():
            return self._error(401, "authentication_error", "invalid x-api-key")
        if self.route not in ("/v1/messages", "/v1/messages/count_tokens"):
            return self._error(404, "not_found_error", f"no route {self.route}")
        body = self._body()
        if body is None:
            return
        if dump := os.environ.get("ARIS_SERVER_DUMP"):
            path = Path(dump) / f"{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}-{new_id('req')}.json"
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text(json.dumps(body, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
        engine = self.server.engine
        name = body.get("model") or engine.spec.name
        if name != engine.spec.name and name in self.server.models:
            return self._error(400, "invalid_request_error",
                               f"model {name!r} is configured but not loaded (loaded: {engine.spec.name!r})")
        spec = engine.spec if name not in self.server.models else resolve(name, self.server.models)
        try:
            p = plan(body, spec, guards=self.server.guards)
        except RequestError as e:
            return self._reject(e)
        if self.route.endswith("count_tokens"):
            return self._json(200, {"input_tokens": engine.count_tokens(p)})
        p.context = _fit_window(p.context, getattr(engine, "max_context", None))
        try:
            fit_context(p, engine.count_tokens(p))
        except RequestError as e:
            return self._reject(e)
        if body.get("stream"):
            self._stream(name, p)
        else:
            self._complete(name, p)

    # --- generation -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _complete(self, name, p):
        t0 = time.time()
        run = self.server.engine.run(p)
        builder = MessageBuilder(run.tool_parser, parse_tools(p))
        finish, n, checked = None, 0, time.time()
        for pieces, finish, n in run.pieces:
            for piece in pieces:
                builder.feed(piece.state, piece.text)
            if time.time() - checked > DISCONNECT_CHECK_SECONDS:
                checked = time.time()
                if self._client_gone():
                    run.stop()
                    logging.info("client disconnected after %d tokens; generation stopped", n)
                    return
        _, reason = builder.finish(finish, p.context_capped)
        msg = _message(name, builder.blocks, reason, run, n)
        self._json(200, msg)
        _log(name, p, run, n, builder, reason, t0, self.server.engine)

    def _stream(self, name, p):
        t0 = time.time()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("request-id", new_id("req"))
        self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream")
        self.send_header("cache-control", "no-cache")
        self.send_header("connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.flush()

        last_write = [time.time()]

        def write(events):
            for e in events:
                self.wfile.write(sse(e))
            self.wfile.flush()
            last_write[0] = time.time()

        holder: list[MessageBuilder] = []
        last_note = [time.time()]

        def progress(done, total):
            logging.debug("prompt %d/%d", done, total)
            if holder and time.time() - last_note[0] > PROGRESS_SECONDS:
                last_note[0] = time.time()
                write(holder[0].note(progress_note(done, total)))
            else:
                write([{"type": "ping"}])

        run = None
        try:
            write([{"type": "ping"}])
            run = self.server.engine.run(p, on_progress=progress)
            builder = MessageBuilder(run.tool_parser, parse_tools(p))
            holder.append(builder)
            start = _message(name, [], None, run, 0)
            write([{"type": "message_start", "message": start}])
            finish, n = None, 0
            for pieces, finish, n in run.pieces:
                events = []
                for piece in pieces:
                    events += builder.feed(piece.state, piece.text)
                if not events and time.time() - last_write[0] > HEARTBEAT_SECONDS:
                    events = [{"type": "ping"}]
                if events:
                    write(events)
            events, reason = builder.finish(finish, p.context_capped)
            events.append({"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": reason, "stop_sequence": None},
                           "usage": _usage(run, n)})
            events.append({"type": "message_stop"})
            write(events)
            _log(name, p, run, n, builder, reason, t0, self.server.engine)
        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):
            if run is not None:
                run.stop()
            logging.info("client disconnected; generation stopped")
            return
        except Exception as e:  # report engine failures in-stream; the status line is already sent
            logging.exception("generation failed")
            if _engine_died(self.server.engine):
                # The server exits and is back within seconds. Clients give up on an error event but retry a
                # dropped connection, so drop it and let the retry land on the restarted server.
                _drop(self.connection)
                return
            try:
                write([{"type": "error", "error": {"type": "api_error", "message": str(e)}}])
            except OSError:
                pass


def _fit_window(context: int | None, fits: int | None) -> int | None:
    """Tokens a request's prompt and reply share: the model's context, or less where this machine's memory ends."""
    return min(context or fits, fits) if fits else context


def _engine_died(engine) -> bool:
    generator = getattr(engine, "generator", None)
    return generator is not None and not generator.generation_available()


def _drop(sock):
    try:
        sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0))  # reset, not a clean close
        sock.close()
    except OSError:
        pass


def _usage(run, n):
    return {"input_tokens": run.prompt_tokens - run.cached_tokens, "cache_read_input_tokens": run.cached_tokens,
            "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": n}


def _message(name, blocks, reason, run, n):
    return {"id": new_id("msg"), "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "model": name, "content": blocks,
            "stop_reason": reason, "stop_sequence": None, "usage": _usage(run, n)}


def _log(name, p, run, n, builder, reason, t0, engine=None):
    dt = time.time() - t0
    budget = run.budget[0] if run.budget else None
    think = f" think={budget.n}/{p.think_budget}{' FORCED' if budget.forced else ''}" if budget else ""
    guard = run.guard[0] if getattr(run, "guard", None) else None
    guarded = (f" stuck-call-reminder={p.stuck_repeats}" if p.stuck_repeats else "") + (
        f" loop-breaks={guard.breaks}{' LOOP-STOPPED' if guard.gave_up else ''}"
        if guard and (guard.breaks or guard.gave_up) else "")
    logging.info("%s effort=%s prompt=%d cached=%d out=%d%s%s tools=%d stop=%s %.1fs (%.1f tok/s) %s", name,
                 p.effort, run.prompt_tokens, run.cached_tokens, n, think, guarded, builder.tool_calls, reason, dt,
                 n / dt if dt else 0, Engine.memory())
    if engine is not None:
        engine.adapt_memory()


# ===== guards.py =====
"""Guards against two ways a local model gets stuck in an agent loop, seen in hard agent tasks:

- a stuck tool call: the model makes the same call turn after turn, gets the same result, and learns nothing new
  (one run listed the same folder 20 turns in a row and never wrote a line of code). `stuck_call_repeats` finds it
  in the request; the server then adds a reminder before the model answers.
- looping output: a response that degenerates into one chunk repeated until the token cap (a test line written a
  thousand times, a run of zeros). `LoopGuard` steers the model off the loop, and gives up on a response that keeps
  falling back into it, so it ends the way the token cap would end it, just tens of thousands of tokens sooner.
"""

import json

import mlx.core as mx

STUCK_REPEATS = 3  # the same call with the same result this many times in a row gets a reminder

LOOP_SPAN = 400    # a loop is the last LOOP_SPAN generated tokens being one chunk repeated...
LOOP_CYCLES = 8    # ...at least this many times (so chunks of up to LOOP_SPAN / LOOP_CYCLES tokens)
LOOP_BREAKS = 3    # times the guard steers a response off a loop before it ends the response instead
# Generated tokens are read back from the GPU this many at a time. Reading each one as it comes would stall every
# decode step (the CPU couldn't queue the next step while the last finished); in batches they're long computed.
LOOP_READ_EVERY = 32

# Tokens the guard never blocks: they close what the model is doing (its thinking, a tool call, the turn), and
# blocking one could trap the model inside it.
ENDING_TEXTS = ("</think>", "</tool_call>", "<|im_end|>", "<|endoftext|>")


def stuck_call_note(repeats: int) -> str:
    return (f"You've made this exact tool call {repeats} times in a row and got the same result each time. Running "
            "it again won't tell you anything new: use the result you already have and take the next step.")


def _flat(content) -> str:
    """A tool result's content as text, for comparing two results exactly."""
    if content is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    if isinstance(content, list):
        return "\n".join(b.get("text", "") if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text"
                         else json.dumps(b, sort_keys=True) for b in content)
    return json.dumps(content, sort_keys=True)


def _typed(message) -> bool:
    """The user wrote something in this message besides tool results (Claude Code's reminders don't count)."""
    content = message.get("content")
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return bool(content.strip())
    return any(isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text"
               and not b.get("text", "").lstrip().startswith("<system-reminder>") for b in content or [])


def _step(assistant, user):
    """One step of the tool loop, as compared between turns: each call's name and input with its result. None when
    the pair isn't the model's tool calls answered by their results alone."""
    if assistant.get("role") != "assistant" or user.get("role") != "user":
        return None
    if not isinstance(assistant.get("content"), list) or not isinstance(user.get("content"), list) or _typed(user):
        return None
    calls = [b for b in assistant["content"] if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_use"]
    results = {b.get("tool_use_id"): b for b in user["content"] if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_result"}
    if not calls or any(c.get("id") not in results for c in calls):
        return None
    return tuple((c.get("name"), json.dumps(c.get("input") or {}, sort_keys=True), _flat(results[c["id"]].get("content")),
                  bool(results[c["id"]].get("is_error"))) for c in calls)


def stuck_call_repeats(messages) -> int:
    """How many times in a row the conversation's latest tool step was made: the same tool call(s), with the same
    input, answered with the same result(s). 0 unless the request answers the model's own tool calls."""
    turns = [m for m in messages or [] if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("role") in ("user", "assistant")]
    k, latest, repeats = len(turns) - 1, None, 0
    while k >= 1:
        step = _step(turns[k - 1], turns[k])
        if step is None or (latest is not None and step != latest):
            break
        latest, repeats, k = step, repeats + 1, k - 2
    return repeats


class LoopGuard:
    """Logits processor. Watches the tokens a response generates; once the last `span` of them are one chunk
    repeated at least `cycles` times, it blocks the token that would continue the chunk, so the model has to write
    something else. After `breaks` of those, the next loop sets `gave_up` instead, and the engine ends the response
    as the token cap would (there is no point generating thousands more tokens of the same chunk).

    A loop is found in O(span / cycles) per token: runs[p] counts how many of the latest tokens each equal the token
    p places before them, so the last `span` tokens repeat with period p once runs[p] >= span - p. Tokens are read
    `read_every` at a time (see LOOP_READ_EVERY), so a loop is caught up to that many tokens late."""

    def __init__(self, exempt: frozenset[int] = frozenset(), span: int = LOOP_SPAN, cycles: int = LOOP_CYCLES,
                 breaks: int = LOOP_BREAKS, read_every: int = LOOP_READ_EVERY):
        self.span, self.allowed, self.exempt, self.read_every = span, breaks, exempt, read_every
        self.max_period = max(1, span // cycles)
        self.recent: list[int] = []
        self.pending: list = []
        self.runs = [0] * (self.max_period + 1)
        self.breaks = 0
        self.gave_up = False

    def _period(self) -> int | None:
        for p in range(1, self.max_period + 1):
            if self.runs[p] >= self.span - p:
                return p
        return None

    def _push(self, token: int) -> None:
        recent = self.recent
        recent.append(token)
        if len(recent) > self.max_period + 1:
            del recent[0]
        runs = self.runs
        for p in range(1, len(recent)):
            runs[p] = runs[p] + 1 if recent[-1 - p] == token else 0

    def __call__(self, tokens, logits):
        if self.gave_up or tokens is None or len(tokens) == 0:
            return logits
        self.pending.append(tokens[-1])
        if len(self.pending) < self.read_every:
            return logits
        for token in mx.concatenate([t.reshape(-1) for t in self.pending]).tolist():
            self._push(int(token))
        self.pending.clear()
        p = self._period()
        if p is None:
            return logits
        self.runs = [0] * (self.max_period + 1)
        if self.breaks >= self.allowed:
            self.gave_up = True
            return logits
        self.breaks += 1
        continuing = self.recent[-p]  # what the chunk would put next
        if continuing in self.exempt:
            return logits
        return mx.where(mx.arange(logits.shape[-1]) == continuing, mx.array(-mx.inf, logits.dtype), logits)


def loop_exempt_ids(tokenizer) -> frozenset[int]:
    """The tokenizer's ids for the tokens `LoopGuard` never blocks: end of turn, of thinking, of a tool call."""
    ids = set(getattr(tokenizer, "eos_token_ids", None) or [])
    texts = set(ENDING_TEXTS)
    for attr in ("think_end", "tool_call_end"):
        try:
            if isinstance(text := getattr(tokenizer, attr, None), str):
                texts.add(text)
        except Exception:  # some tokenizer wrappers raise for a feature the model doesn't have
            pass
    for text in texts:
        try:
            encoded = tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if len(encoded) == 1:
            ids.add(encoded[0])
    return frozenset(ids)


# ===== budget.py =====
"""Think budget: close a model's reasoning on a complete thought once it has used its allowance."""

import mlx.core as mx


class ThinkBudget:
    """Logits processor. Counts generated tokens while thinking. Past `budget`, outside a code fence, a paragraph
    break becomes a single newline and the end-of-thinking token is forced after the next newline; `overrun` tokens
    later it closes regardless (an open fence, or a line that never ends: models can loop in place). Inert once
    thinking has ended.

    Ending on a single newline matters: chat templates re-render past reasoning as `text\\n</think>`, so a turn that
    closed after a paragraph break (`text\\n\\n</think>`) no longer matches its own prompt cache, and the next turn
    re-reads everything from that point."""

    def __init__(self, budget: int, end_id: int, newline_id: int, paragraph_ids: frozenset[int],
                 fence_counts: dict[int, int], overrun: int = 1024):
        self.budget, self.end_id, self.newline_id, self.overrun = budget, end_id, newline_id, overrun
        self.paragraph_ids, self.fence_counts = paragraph_ids, fence_counts
        self.n = self.fences = 0
        self.done = self.forced = False
        self._paragraphs = None

    def _only(self, token_id, logits):
        mask = mx.arange(logits.shape[-1]) == token_id
        return mx.broadcast_to(mx.where(mask, mx.array(0.0, logits.dtype), mx.array(-mx.inf, logits.dtype)),
                               logits.shape)

    def __call__(self, tokens, logits):
        if self.done or tokens is None or len(tokens) == 0:
            return logits
        last = int(tokens[-1].item())
        if last == self.end_id:
            self.done = True
            return logits
        self.n += 1
        self.fences += self.fence_counts.get(last, 0)
        if self.n < self.budget:
            return logits
        hard = self.n >= self.budget + self.overrun
        if self.fences % 2 and not hard:
            return logits
        if last == self.newline_id:
            self.done = self.forced = True
            return self._only(self.end_id, logits)
        if hard:
            return self._only(self.newline_id, logits)
        # A paragraph break the model would take becomes a single newline, which then closes thinking.
        if self._paragraphs is None:
            ids = sorted(self.paragraph_ids)
            self._paragraphs = mx.array(ids) if ids else None
        if self._paragraphs is None:
            return logits
        flat = logits.reshape(-1, logits.shape[-1])
        merged = mx.logaddexp(flat[:, self.newline_id], mx.logsumexp(flat[:, self._paragraphs], axis=-1))
        flat[:, self._paragraphs] = -mx.inf
        flat[:, self.newline_id] = merged
        return flat.reshape(logits.shape)


class BudgetTokens:
    """Per-tokenizer lookups the processor needs, computed once per model."""

    def __init__(self, tokenizer):
        end = tokenizer.think_end_tokens if hasattr(tokenizer, "think_end_tokens") else None
        self.end_id = end[0] if end and len(end) == 1 else None
        newline = tokenizer.encode("\n", add_special_tokens=False) if hasattr(tokenizer, "encode") else []
        self.newline_id = newline[0] if len(newline) == 1 else None
        self.paragraph_ids, self.fence_counts = set(), {}
        decode = tokenizer.decode
        for i in range(len(tokenizer.vocab) if hasattr(tokenizer, "vocab") else tokenizer.vocab_size):
            text = decode([i])
            if text.endswith("\n\n"):
                self.paragraph_ids.add(i)
            if "```" in text:
                self.fence_counts[i] = text.count("```")
        self.paragraph_ids = frozenset(self.paragraph_ids)

    def make(self, budget: int) -> ThinkBudget | None:
        if budget <= 0 or self.end_id is None or self.newline_id is None:
            return None
        return ThinkBudget(budget, self.end_id, self.newline_id, self.paragraph_ids, self.fence_counts)
